# 7. Generated TypeScript

The language projector renders the structured code-body authority into executable TypeScript.

```typescript
// @generated by semantic-kernel/declarative-typescript.v1
// projection-id: project-scenario-atomicity-body
// scenario-id: reject-a-scenario-with-multiple-obligations
// obligation-id: scenario-carries-one-obligation
// responsibility-id: evaluates-scenario-atomicity
// signal-id: scenario-atomicity
// DO NOT EDIT.

import type {
  EvaluateScenarioAtomicityContext,
  ScenarioAtomicitySignal
} from "../types/scenario-atomicity.type.js";

export async function evaluatesScenarioAtomicity(
  context: EvaluateScenarioAtomicityContext
): Promise<ScenarioAtomicitySignal> {
  return await context.edges.invokes(
    "evaluate-scenario-atomicity",
    context
  );
}
```

This file is not a new source of software meaning.

It is the Node/TypeScript embodiment of previously admitted:

```text
scenario expectation
semantic authority
file-body contract
code-body projection authority
```

```text

EXECUTABLE PROJECTION

Generated TypeScript:
```

The file may execute the admitted responsibility.

It may not redefine:

* the scenario;
* the obligation;
* the responsibility;
* the signal;
* the semantic authority;
* the expected body lineage; or
* the proof boundary.

# Where the Generated Marker Came From

## Code-body authority node

```json

  "generatedHeader": {
```

```typescript
// @generated by semantic-kernel/declarative-typescript.v1

```

## Why it matters

The generated marker tells the student and platform agent:

```text
This file was produced by a declared projector.

This file should not be changed directly.

Changes must begin above the projection boundary.
```

# Where the Scenario ID Came From

## Expected body lineage

```json

}
```

## This becomes

```typescript
// scenario-id: reject-a-scenario-with-multiple-obligations
```

## Why it matters

This tag identifies the scenario that owns the body.

The lineage is:

```text
Scenario
    ↓
Expectation
    ↓

```

A generated body without a scenario identity cannot prove which behavior it was projected to satisfy.

# Where the Obligation ID Came From

## Scenario expectation

```json
{
  "expectedObligation": {
    "obligationId": "scenario-carries-one-obligation"
  }
}
```

## This becomes

```typescript
// obligation-id: scenario-carries-one-obligation
```

## Why it matters

The obligation tag states the semantic boundary the code body must remain within.

The body may:

```text
evaluate whether the scenario is atomic
```

The body may not:

```text
rewrite the scenario
repair the feature
move obligations into tables
generate replacement authority
aggregate unrelated proof
```

The obligation tag makes semantic overreach visible during review.

---

# What the Generated Body Does

The body performs one mechanical responsibility:

```text
Accept one immutable context
    ↓
Invoke one admitted semantic authority
    ↓
Return one scenario-atomicity signal
```

The body does not determine:

```text
What counts as an obligation
Whether two obligations are independent
How tables are classified
What RED means
What GREEN means
Whether the scenario should be repaired
How the signal DTO is constructed
```

Those meanings were declared earlier.

---

# What the Generated Body Must Never Contain

A conforming body must not grow into this:

```typescript
export async function evaluatesScenarioAtomicity(
  context: EvaluateScenarioAtomicityContext
): Promise<ScenarioAtomicitySignal> {
  const clauses = countScenarioClauses(context);
  const tables = inspectScenarioTables(context);
  const obligations = inferIndependentObligations(context);
  const rewritten = convertObligationsToTable(context);
  const proof = aggregateScenarioProof(context);

  return {
    clauses,
    tables,
    obligations,
    rewritten,
    proof
  };
}
```

That body exposes several separate responsibilities:

```text
count clauses
inspect tables
infer obligations
rewrite feature authority
aggregate proof
```

It no longer embodies one atomic responsibility.

A repository guard should return RED before admitting it.

Possible findings:

```text
MULTIPLE_RESPONSIBILITIES_BELOW_ATOMIC_SCENARIO
SEMANTIC_FAN_OUT_EXCEEDED
UNAUTHORIZED_REMEDIATION_BEHAVIOR
MULTIPLE_SIGNALS_BELOW_ATOMIC_SCENARIO
AUTHORED_DTO_CONSTRUCTION_DETECTED
```

# Generated Code Freshness

The generated file must be checked against the current projection authority.

```text
Current authority bytes
    ↓
Re-run language projector
    ↓
Produce expected artifact bytes
    ↓
Compare with repository artifact
```

Possible outcomes:

```text
Bytes equal
    → PROJECTED_BODY_CURRENT

Bytes differ
    → PROJECTED_BODY_STALE

Generated marker missing
    → GENERATED_BODY_MARKER_MISSING

Projection ID differs
    → PROJECTION_ID_MISMATCH

Semantic identity differs
    → SEMANTIC_AUTHORITY_ID_MISMATCH
```

The body is trusted only when it is reproducible from current admitted authority.

The generated body should be accompanied by projection testimony.

```json
{
  "receiptType": "code-projection-receipt.v1",
  "projectionId": "project-scenario-atomicity-body",
  "projectorId": "semantic-kernel/declarative-typescript.v1",
  "targetId": "typescript-esm",
  "authoritySha256": "sha256:...",

    {
      "path": "src/runtime/evaluates-scenario-atomicity.ts",
      "sha256": "sha256:..."
    }
  ],
  "semanticSubject": {
    "scenarioId": "reject-a-scenario-with-multiple-obligations",
    "obligationId": "scenario-carries-one-obligation",
    "responsibilityId": "evaluates-scenario-atomicity",
    "signalId": "scenario-atomicity",
    "semanticAuthorityId": "evaluate-scenario-atomicity"
  },

```

The receipt proves:

```text
which projection authority was used
which projector rendered the code
which target profile applied
which artifact path was produced
which bytes were emitted
which semantic subject owns the body
```

The receipt does not yet prove that the runtime behavior is correct.

It proves that the code artifact came from the declared projection authority.

# Platform-Agent Requirements

When the platform agent creates or inspects this file, it must verify:

```text
The generated marker exists.

The projection ID matches admitted authority.

The scenario ID matches the expected lineage.

The obligation ID matches the scenario expectation.

The responsibility ID matches the semantic authority.

The signal ID matches the expected signal.

The function name matches the naming projection.

The parameter and return types match body authority.

The invoked semantic identity is exact.

The body contains no undeclared syntax.

The artifact bytes match fresh projection output.
```

The platform agent must not treat generated code as permission to reverse-engineer or expand the design.

It must move upward to authority whenever a change is needed.

# Student Lesson

Students should be able to point at every line of this file and answer:

```text
Where did this come from?

Which authority node declared it?

Which semantic subject does it represent?

How is its freshness proven?
```

The central rule is:

> Every meaningful part of generated code must have an admitted origin, and every generated byte must be reproducible from current projection authority.

```text
Authority declares.

Projector renders.

Code executes.

Receipt proves origin.

Conformance proves behavior.
```
